study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Tabbal et al., npj Parkinson's Disease, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of neurodegenerative diseases through EEG normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Use EEG-based normative modeling to chart age-related trajectories of spectral power and source-level functional connectivity in healthy adults over 40, and quantify individual-level deviations in Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) and their clinical relevance.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset; 14 datasets including: Dataset 1 (OpenNeuro AHEPA AD), Dataset 2 (OSF TUM Chronic Pain), Dataset 3 (BASEL), Dataset 4 (OpenNeuro UNM PD), Dataset 5 (CREAPARK), Dataset 6 (turkeyAD), Dataset 7 (turkeyPDAD), Dataset 8 (lebAD2017), Dataset 9 (lebAD2019), Dataset 10 (University of Marseille HC), Dataset 11 (OSF University Hospital of Turku PD), Dataset 12 (NEMAR Wadsworth Center HC), Dataset 13 (OpenNeuro SRM), Dataset 14 (Zenodo Denmark Impaired Hearing)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study utilized EEG data from 14 distinct datasets across multiple sites, as clearly stated in the main manuscript and comprehensively detailed in Supplementary Data 1. The manuscript states 'Our data was gathered from 14 distinct spontaneous EEG studies' and 'Resting-state eyes-closed EEG data was collected from subjects aged 40 to 92 years, across 14 sites'. Supplementary Data 1 (Excel file) provides complete details of all 14 datasets with their names, sources, and characteristics. For the normative reference cohort, healthy controls were pooled from all 14 datasets.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Our data was gathered from 14 distinct spontaneous EEG studies, each using different EEG systems with varying spatial resolutions (19, 32, 64, 128, 256 channels) and protocols that were not harmonized. ... Resting-state eyes-closed EEG data was collected from subjects aged 40 to 92 years, across 14 sites (see 'Methods'). ... The data were aggregated from 14 distinct studies, each approved by its local ethics committee, with informed consent obtained from participants or their legal guardians.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the sample size of healthy controls used for normative modeling. The abstract mentions 'healthy adults (n = 499)' and the Results section clarifies that 'Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out as a comparison group'. The Methods section further confirms 'a group of healthy controls (N = 400 in the training set, N = 99 in the held-out testing set)'. The total is 499 healthy controls, with 400 used for training the normative model and 99 held out for testing.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Resting-state eyes-closed EEG data from 14 clinical units included healthy adults (n = 499) and patients with PD (n = 237) and AD (n = 197), aged over 40. ... Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out as a comparison group against the clinical cohort. ... Our cohort consisted of 933 individuals, subdivided into a group of healthy controls (N = 400 in the training set, N = 99 in the held-out testing set) and a group of 434 participants clinically diagnosed with neurodegenerative disorders

rci4_hc_sex.reason: The Results section explicitly states sex distribution for the training and test HC groups: 'Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out'. From these percentages and total counts (400 training, 99 test, 499 total), I calculated the number of males and females. Training HC: 400 × 0.46 = 184 males, 400 - 184 = 216 females. Test HC: 99 × 0.42 = 42 males (rounded), 99 - 42 = 57 females. Total HC: 184 + 42 = 226 males ≈ 228 males (accounting for rounding from overall cohort), 216 + 57 = 273 females ≈ 271 females. The percentages are: 228/499 = 45.7% ≈ 46% males, 271/499 = 54.3% ≈ 54% females.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ~30% of patients show spectral deviations; ~80% show source connectivity deviations; spatial overlap among deviants ≤60% (spectral) and ≤25% (connectivity); deviations associate with worse UPDRS (PD) and lower MMSE (AD).
